articles.title: No, collagen won’t make your wrinkles disappear - video

source.name: Presented by Madeleine Finlay , produced by Madeleine Finlay, Ellie Sans and Jacob Liebenberg , the executive producer was Ellie Bury

articles.description: Collagen powders, gummies and pills have boomed in popularity in recent years boosted by claims that they smooth wrinkles, promote glossy hair and help with joint pain. Amid the noise it can be hard to figure out whether there’s any actual science behind the promise of looking younger for longer. Luckily Dr Xand van Tulleken has spent the past three years writing Make me well: a quest to understand the confusing world of wellness, and his chapter on collagen dives deep into the evidence. articles.description: After Brentford overcame Reading to reach the Carabao Cup fourth round, head coach Keith Andrews believes the video assistant referee (VAR) is preventing referees from making decisions in matches.

articles.title: Brook & Baker shine as England crush Sri Lanka
articles.description: Harry Brook hit 114 not out in the first innings set up England with a total of 254 proving to difficult for Sri Lanka to chase leading to a England win by 119 runs after bowling out Sri Lanka.

articles.title: Sweeney ad a barrier for girls in sport - Hunt
articles.description: British sprinter Amy Hunt says she is concerned about the controversial advert starring Sydney Sweeney being part of a "barrier" to girls' participation in sport.

articles.title: Tuchel regrets not eating Azteca turf after win over Mexico
articles.description: Thomas Tuchel regrets not eating any of the grass at the Azteca Stadium after England's epic World Cup win against Mexico.

articles.title: Messi in Argentina squad for farewell friendly
articles.description: Argentina name Lionel Messi in their squad for a friendly against Benin in October in a match which is set to be the forward's farewell to international football.

articles.title: VAR did not even consider if Fernandez was offside - Webb
articles.description: Referees' chief Howard Webb has admitted that the video assistant referee (VAR) did not even consider whether Enzo Fernandez was offside for Erling Haaland's controversial winner in Sunday's Manchester derby.
